title: The North Face Manta Ray 33 review: a roomy T-shaped tent that's quiet in wind
dek: A three-person tent with 8.84 mm DAC Featherlite poles that snap into Jake's Foot sockets. Owners praise its space and stability, and warn about rain when the doors are open.
subject: The North Face Manta Ray 33
verdict: The Manta Ray 33 is a freestanding three-person tent with a T-shaped floor, big vestibules and a gear loft, and owners say it's silent and steady in 40–50 mph wind. The doors let rain in when they're open, and it only comes with half the stakes it needs.
bestFor: Two people plus gear, or three on summer trips, who want space and a quick pitch.
notFor: Rainy trips where you'll be in and out often, or minimal-weight backpacking.
pros: Owner reports no flapping or noise in 40–50 mph wind
Big vestibules, interior wings and a gear loft
Ball-end poles snap into sockets for a fast, solo pitch
Good ventilation; owner reports no condensation problems
cons: Rain pours in when the doors are open
Comes with 8 stakes for 16 stake points
Discontinued, and footprints are hard to find
body:
## The short version

The Manta Ray 33 is a freestanding three-person tent from around 2009 with a T-shaped floor that widens at the head end. Its three DAC Featherlite poles are 8.84 mm, and their ball-shaped ends plug into plastic sockets The North Face called Jake's Foot. Owners rate it highly for space and wind stability.

## Weather

The main owner review tested it through several rainy weekends and stayed dry, apart from one leak where feet touched the wall. In 40 to 50 mph wind and thunderstorms it had no flapping and no noise. A second owner agrees it's waterproof with the doors closed, but says rain pours in when they're open. Support the door when you go in and out in wet weather.

## Space

It's rated for three, but owners say it's most comfortable for two with gear. Two large vestibules, interior nightstand wings and a gear loft add storage, and the vestibules fit packs, shoes and even a small dog.

## Setup

Owners find it fast and easy, even solo and in wind, with color-coded clips and no instructions needed. Getting the clip tension right takes a pitch or two to learn. With 16 stake-out points, it's very stable once fully staked, but it only comes with 8 stakes, and they lack pull loops.

## Poles and parts

The Manta Ray 33 uses **3 poles**, **8.84 mm** tubing, **DAC Featherlite**.

The poles end in balls that seat into Jake's Foot sockets at the corners, so a replacement needs the same ball-end tips as well as the right length and 8.84 mm diameter.

The North Face doesn't publish pole lengths. To match a replacement, lay your pole out straight, measure tip to tip, count the sections, and read the diameter printed near a joint (or use calipers). Then search the Manta Ray 33 in our [pole and parts finder](/poles?model=Manta%20Ray%2033), compare against measured stock in the [pole size chart](/poles/sizes), or search by measurement in [find a pole by size](/poles/size).

## Bottom line

A used Manta Ray 33 is a roomy, quiet tent for two or three. Bring 16 stakes and plan your entries in the rain.
